text: A US passport needs a visa, applied for before you travel; the one exception is a stay of thirty days or fewer on Phú Quốc, arriving and leaving the island directly.
The e-visa costs twenty-five dollars for a single entry or fifty for multiple entries, paid by bank transfer on the official site, evisa.gov.vn, and nowhere else.
Validity runs up to ninety days, and the period granted is usually exactly the one you asked for.
Processing usually takes three to five working days once the Immigration Department has the completed application and the payment, and longer during surges and holidays.
Your entry and exit points must match the ports you selected on the application.
An e-visa cannot be renewed or extended from inside Vietnam.
An e-visa is valid at eighty-three designated gates — seventeen airports, twenty-seven land crossings and thirty-nine seaports — which covers every international airport in the country.

A separate pre-arrival declaration is filed online, free, within the three days before you land; the State Department calls it required for air arrivals on a foreign passport and Vietnam's own portal calls it advisory.
The passport must be valid for six months beyond the arrival date, with blank pages for stamps.

A US driver's licence and an International Driving Permit are both invalid in Vietnam; driving without a Vietnamese licence can mean a fine, arrest or jail, and renting a motorbike without one is illegal.
After an accident without a valid licence, travel insurance may not pay your medical bills.
the law requires zero alcohol while driving, not a threshold.
The State Department places Vietnam at Level 1, Exercise Normal Precautions, the lowest of its four levels, in an advisory dated June 24, 2026.
there is no limit on the currency you carry in or out, but anything over fifteen million đồng or five thousand US dollars must be declared, in both directions.
No vaccination is required to enter Vietnam; the CDC recommends Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B and typhoid for most travellers.
transmission is rural only, and the CDC lists none in Hanoi, Saigon, Đà Nẵng, Hải Phòng, Nha Trang or Quy Nhơn.
Vietnam keeps one time zone, seven hours ahead of UTC with no daylight saving, which puts it twelve hours ahead of the East Coast in winter and eleven in summer.
The only nonstop between the United States and Vietnam is Vietnam Airlines' San Francisco to Ho Chi Minh City service, and there is no nonstop to Hanoi.
In 2027 Tết falls on 6 February, with the official holiday running from 4 to 10 February.
In 2027 National Day runs from 2 to 5 September.

Vietnam requires a valid visa, a residence card or Immigration Department approval to leave as well as to enter, and if you cannot leave on time for any reason, including a medical emergency, you will likely pay overstay fines and face delays getting permission to go.
The emergency numbers are 113 for the traffic police and 115 for an ambulance.
every visitor's overnight address must be registered with the local police, which the hotel does from the passport at check-in and a homestay host is responsible for.

Police sometimes test blood for drugs, a substance used legally in another country can still lead to arrest and a long sentence if it is in your system, and ingredients in some common prescriptions, including ADHD medicines, may be illegal here.
The Huế to Đà Nẵng train runs about two and a half to three hours along the coast and over the Hải Vân Pass, sea side if you ask for it.
the Reunification line covers Hanoi to Saigon in roughly thirty-two to thirty-six hours.
every rider and every passenger on a motorbike must wear a helmet with the strap fastened, the pillion included.
under Vietnam's own traffic law, driving without the licence it requires is a listed prohibited act, and so is handing the keys to someone who lacks one.
red means stop here, and a right turn on red is lawful only where an arrow or a sign says so.
on the Cambodian side an e-visa works only at Bavet, the road crossing on the Saigon–Phnom Penh bus route, so the river exit at Châu Đốc needs a Cambodian visa obtained another way.
there have been deaths and serious illness in Vietnam from drinks containing methanol, bought in licensed bars, shops and hotels in tourist areas, and methanol cannot be identified by taste or smell.
you must enter and leave Vietnam on the same passport, and fly domestically on it too.

a US-citizen child of Vietnamese parentage may need a Vietnamese passport or a Vietnamese exit visa to leave the country, and the requirement attaches to parentage, not to the passport the child arrived on.
a Vietnamese minor, a dual US citizen included, needs notarised consent to travel without a parent or guardian, and children have been stopped at departure without it.

an overseas Vietnamese, or the spouse or child of one, can hold a visa-exemption paper valid for up to five years that admits them for six months at a time, on proof of Vietnamese origin or of the relationship.
the road from Hanoi to the bay has been about two and a half hours since the expressway opened in 2018, which is the same morning Ninh Bình costs.
the port authority stops every tourist vessel at once when a storm is forecast, day boats and overnight cruises alike, and the operators can only refund or reschedule.
prices, quotes and payment inside Vietnam are in đồng by law, with dollar pricing confined to listed cases such as duty-free shops.
the duty is the host's, within twelve hours of your arrival, and the statute asks for a declaration, not the surrender of the passport.
